summary: Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, studying under Julius Jolly (~1912–1913). He served as Professor of Iranian Studies at Deccan College (~1939–1942) and Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (~1954–1956).

Irawati Karve specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Huzurpaga, Fergusson College, and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. She served at Deccan College (~1939–1970) as Professor of Sociology and Anthropology and at the University of Pennsylvania (~1959–1960).

Irfan Habib is a historian working in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University (~1947–1953), and New College (~1954–1957), and served as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1953.

Irina Anatolyevna Svetovidova was an Indologist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1950–1955). She was a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Leningrad Oriental Institute (1957–1968) and taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1965–1968).

Irving Babbitt worked in philosophy, studying at Harvard, Williams College, the University of Paris, and EPHE. He served as Instructor in Romance Languages at Williams College (1893–1894) and Assistant Professor at Harvard University (1894–1912).

Isaac Schapera worked in history and archaeology, studying at Cándido Candi, the University of Cape Town, and the LSE under Bronisław Malinowski. He held posts at the University of Chicago (~1948–1949), LSE (~1950–1969), and University of Toronto (~1953–1954).

Isaak Jakob Schmidt was a scholar of Tibetology, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at the University of Rostock. He served at the Russian Bible Society (~1812–1826) and Saint Petersburg State University, and was a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy specializes in Tibetology. She studied at ULB, LASSAAD, Tibet University, EPHE under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert, Harvard, and Qinghai Nationalities University. In 2007, she became Full Professor at Laval University.

Isabelle Onians is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Oxford by 2002 and served as an editor at the Clay Sanskrit Library (attested 2007).

Isabelle Ratié works in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Paris 1 and EPHE, learning under Lyne Bansat-Boudon and Alexis Sanderson. Her posts include the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Leipzig, Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and Collège de France (2025).

Isaiah Berlin was a philosopher and historian who studied at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1928–1932). He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Oxford from around 1932 to 1975.

Isaline Blew Horner was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Newnham College, Cambridge, studying under Kenneth J. Saunders and Caroline Rhys Davids. She held librarian and governance roles at Newnham and served as Hon. Secretary of the Pali Text Society (1942–1981).
Isamu Kanaji was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held posts as professor at Shitennoji University and Shitennoji Junior College, both attested in 1976.

Isao Nishitani works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He held a post at Sennyu-ji (attested 2016) and serves as an associate professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026).
Iselin Frydenlund works in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2016, she was attested as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and a research fellow at the University of Oslo.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He held posts at Fort William College (1841–1846, 1849), Sanskrit College (1846–1849), and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1851).

Isidor Isaac Scheftelowitz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Königsberg under Adalbert Bezzenberger. He held posts at the University of Cologne (1919; 1923–1933) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1933–1934).

Ismael Quiles Sánchez studied philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies at institutions including Colegio Máximo de San Ignacio and San José. He served as Visiting Professor at Georgetown University (1950–1965) and Vice-Rector (1956–1962) and Prorector (1965–1974) at Universidad del Salvador.

Iso Kern is a philosopher and sinologist. He studied at KU Leuven, the University of Freiburg, Heidelberg University, and National Taiwan University. He held academic positions at KU Leuven, Heidelberg University, the University of Zurich, the University of Fribourg, and the University of Bern.
Issaien Ikeyama was a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at both Shitennoji Junior College and Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).
